headline: Robert Pattinson is the new Bond. Bezos helped pick him.
summary: Robert Pattinson will be the seventh James Bond, after Daniel Craig. It is the first Bond made under Amazon, and Jeff Bezos told Semafor on Tuesday he was "heavily involved" in the choice. Five finalists did screen tests in full costume on real sets. The panel first leaned toward someone less famous. Then, Bezos said, it was obvious.

cover_question.q: Why does the boss get to pick Bond?

cover_answer: Amazon makes the films now, and Bezos founded Amazon.
table_question: The famous kid or the new kid: who gets the lead in the play?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A movie company picked a new actor to play James Bond, a pretend spy. Five actors tried out in the real costumes on the real movie sets, like dressing up to try out for the school play. They chose Robert Pattinson. That is the whole story: an actor got a job.
5-7.why: At seven the dress-up tryout is the whole story, and it ends with somebody getting the part.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script makes the tryout the thing: costumes, a set, five actors, one picked. Dressing up for the school play is something they have seen or done. The owner and the money stay out of it. Expect "can I try out?" Not for this one. A play at school works the same way, though.

8-12.script: Amazon makes the Bond films now, and its founder, Jeff Bezos, says he helped pick the new one. Five actors did screen tests in full costume on real sets, like a tryout where everyone runs the same drill. The panel nearly chose someone less famous. Then, Bezos said, it was obvious.
8-12.why: Five tryouts, one drill, one pick: a chain a ten-year-old can run.
8-12.why_long: At ten a child is working out rules and whether adults apply them fairly. The script hands over one chain: five finalists, the same test, a panel that leaned against the famous one, a pick. That is a tryout, and they have stood in one. Expect "so did being famous help or hurt?" Bezos says it nearly hurt. Doubting that is fair.

13-17.script: Should the man who owns the studio pick the actor? Jeff Bezos says he was "heavily involved" in casting Robert Pattinson as Bond, the first under Amazon. Five finalists, and a panel that first leaned away from him as too famous. Second: should fame count for him, or against?
13-17.why: Two true things at seventeen: a fair process, and an owner telling it.
13-17.why_long: At seventeen they can hold two true things: the process sounds fair, and the man describing it owns the studio. The script gives both, then asks whether an owner in the room is a problem and whether fame should count against you. Kuhn: defending a side out loud is how arguing is practised. Expect "does it matter who picks?" It does.

5-7.a: A pretend spy in movies. Different actors have played him. Robert Pattinson is the seventh.

8-12.q: Why does the boss get to pick Bond?
8-12.a: Amazon makes the films now, and Bezos founded Amazon. He watched the tests.

8-12.q: How do you try out to be Bond?
8-12.a: Screen tests: five finalists acted scenes in costume on real sets.

13-17.q: Isn't being famous a reason to pick him?
13-17.a: Bezos says the panel leaned against him for his fame. The tests settled it.

13-17.q: Should the owner be casting at all?
13-17.a: He says he was, and the process was tight. Who else was there isn't said.
